title: Fine structure of the cyclotron resonance in heterobilayers of proximitized graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides
authors: M. A. Rakitskii, K. S. Denisov, N. S. Averkiev
abstract: A monolayer graphene and its Dirac electrons can be equipped with an enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) when proximitized by other van der Waals (vdW) materials, such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). In this work we analyze the cyclotron resonance (CR) absorption of such heterobilayers at quantizing magnetic fields in the presence of proximity-induced spin interactions, including the spin-pseudospin Rashba coupling. We evaluate the spin-textured wave functions of the Landau levels and calculate the absorption spectrum paying special attention to its spin proximity induced modifications. We reveal the formation of a fine double-peak structure of the main interband CR transitions, as well as the presence of additional spin-flip absorption, the combined cyclotron resonance (CCR), centered at different resonant frequencies. The selection rules for CCRs are identified and complemented by the perturbation theory analysis. We also discuss the polarization dependence of the absorption and the proximity-induced emerging magneto-optical responses. Our theory explains the effect of proximity-induced spin interactions for Dirac electrons cyclotron resonance and points out at its experimental verifications.
summary: This theoretical study investigates how proximity effects from TMDs induce spin-orbit coupling in graphene, modifying its cyclotron resonance spectrum. The authors predict characteristic fine double-peak structures and new spin-flip absorption lines (CCRs). These modifications lead to a measurable magneto-optical response, providing a powerful spectroscopic tool for characterizing spin interactions in van der Waals heterostructures.
main_problem: The study analyzes the fine structure of cyclotron resonance (CR) and combined cyclotron resonance (CCR) absorption in heterobilayers formed by proximitizing graphene with transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). The focus is on how proximity-induced spin interactions modify these optical responses.
main_result: The theory predicts a polarization-dependent fine double-peak structure in the main interband CR transitions and identifies additional spin-flip absorption lines corresponding to CCRs. Furthermore, it shows that these effects lead to a measurable Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) signal.
method: The analysis employs an effective Dirac model augmented by proximity terms ($H_{vz}, H_{st}, H_R$) and calculates the optical absorption spectrum using the Kubo–Greenwood formula in the Landau Level basis. Numerical diagonalization is used to incorporate the Rashba coupling effects.
model_or_system: The system is a heterobilayer of graphene proximitized by TMDs, modeled with an effective Hamiltonian including valley-Zeeman ($H_{vz}$), staggered potential ($H_{st}$), and crucial spin-orbit coupling via the Rashba term ($H_R$). The analysis operates in the Landau Level basis derived from minimal coupling.
key_observables: Cyclotron Resonance (CR) absorption spectrum, Combined Cyclotron Resonance (CCR) lines, Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) signal, and polarization dependence ($\sigma^+$ vs $\sigma^-$).
important_parameters: Moderate magnetic fields ($0.5–2$ T), where cyclotron energies dominate proximity terms; the strength of the Rashba coupling ($\lambda_R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the LL basis derived from minimal coupling is sufficient, and it treats the Rashba term perturbatively or within a truncated diagonalization scheme.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate CR/CCR absorption spectra showing fine double-peak structures (Figure 3) and demonstrate selection rules for these transitions. Figure 4 specifically shows resolved CCR lines below main interband CR lines at specific magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and Hamiltonian, details the theoretical methods using LL basis diagonalization, calculates the key observables (CR/CCR absorption), and concludes by interpreting the results in terms of measurable MOKE signals and experimental verifications.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant because it uses optical spectroscopy (CR) to probe subtle quantum phenomena—namely spin-orbit coupling and spin texture—in 2D materials heterostructures, which are key areas for developing spintronic devices.

Spintronics.note: The paper analyzes magneto-optical responses (MOKE signal) arising from proximity-induced spin interactions in a heterostructure, directly connecting quantum optics concepts (CR/absorption spectroscopy) with spintronic phenomena.
